name: PIXELLE SPECIALTY SOLUTIONS LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The closing entity is Pixelle Specialty Solutions, LLC, the grant payee itself, a specialty paper maker owned by H.I.G. Capital. No bankruptcy petition was found and none is claimed in the notice. This is the shutdown of one mill, not a corporate insolvency.
ohio_outcome: The mill closed. Pixelle gave notice on 2025-04-15 of its intent to permanently cease manufacturing operations at the Chillicothe Mill, 232 E. 8th Street, Chillicothe, OH 45601, then revised the first separation date from 2025-06-13 to 2025-08-10 in a letter dated 2025-06-10. The revision says local and state officials actively tried to find a buyer for the facility and failed, and that order volume had fallen sharply while employees were leaving. 780 employees are named on the attached schedule, across roughly 300 union and salaried paper-mill classifications. Three unions were served: OPEIU Local 422 and United Steelworkers Locals 731 and 988. Ohio's register classes the notice as a Closure. JobsOhio's own August 2022 project record for this company is a Ross County project, Advanced Manufacturing, 52 jobs created and 993 retained on an $11,847,833 investment with a $250,000 JobsOhio Workforce Grant; $133,645 of that was paid in cash in FY2023, two and a half years before the mill closed.
source: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services WARN notice, 'Pixelle Specialty Solutions Updated WARN', received 6/10/2025, fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2025/PixelleSpecialtySolutionsUpdatedWARN.pdf (14 pages, letter plus the full affected-job-title schedule). State 2025 WARN table row: Chillicothe/Ross, Closure, 780 affected, layoff date 8/10/2025. data/grants_raw.csv FY2023 row (PIXELLE SPECIALTY SOLUTIONS LLC, EIN 83-1623694, 228 S Main St, Spring Grove, PA, $133,645). data/commitments_norm.csv 2022-Aug row. Google News headlines confirming the aftermath: WOSU, 'Data center and more new tenants expected for shuttered Chillicothe paper mill site', 2026-07-06; NBC4 WCMH, 'Paper manufacturing returning to Chillicothe', 2026-09-28.
notes: The payment address is Pixelle's Spring Grove, Pennsylvania head office, which is why the city-level join missed it. The test that matters is satisfied another way: JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Ross County, the notice is the Chillicothe Mill, Chillicothe is the county seat of Ross, and the mill is Pixelle's only Ross County operation. This is the largest single notice in the batch. A second, separate Pixelle closure notice exists for a different Ohio site, the Fremont converting facility at 2275 Commerce Drive, Fremont, Sandusky County, 61 employees from 2026-12-01, caused by the sale of the carbonless business to a buyer moving production to Wisconsin. That Fremont site is not the funded site and should not be added to this row.
funded_site: Ross County, Ohio (JobsOhio's own 2022-Aug project record); the Chillicothe Mill is Pixelle's only Ross County operation
failed_site: Chillicothe Mill, 232 E. 8th Street, Chillicothe, OH 45601 (Ross County)
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed closure of the funded site, and lead with it: 780 jobs is the largest failure in this batch.

name: FCA US LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is FCA US LLC, the grant payee itself, a subsidiary of Stellantis N.V. The HR manager who signed both notices uses a stellantis.com address. The parent is solvent; these are mass layoffs at one plant.
ohio_outcome: Two mass layoffs at the funded plant, which stayed open. The 2023-12-07 notice covers the Toledo Assembly Plant at 4400 Chrysler Drive, Toledo, OH 43608: 1,225 job losses from 2024-02-05, made up of 131 Production Operators and Team Members and 1,094 Supplemental Employees. The 2024-11-06 notice covers the same complex: 1,134 job losses from 2025-01-05, made up of 1,095 Production Operators and Team Members, 14 Team Leaders, 21 Repair and 4 Office, Clerical and Engineering, caused by a change from a two-shift to a one-shift operating pattern at Toledo South Assembly plus the elimination of tag relief. Both letters say the job losses are permanent, exceed six months, and that the plant is not closing. Employees are UAW Local 12 and have bumping rights. JobsOhio's own records are two Lucas County projects: August 2017, 679 jobs created and 4,485 retained on a $429,000,000 investment with a $1,000,000 Economic Development Grant and a $3,000,000 Workforce Grant; and June 2019, 94 created and 5,164 retained on a $273,300,000 investment with a $553,500 Economic Development Grant. $4,540,017 was paid in cash across FY2018 to FY2021.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full: jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/FCAUS.pdf (letter of 2023-12-07, received 12/07/2023, with Attachment A) and dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2024/FCAUS2.pdf (letter of 2024-11-06, with Attachment A). Both signed by Jason Nault, Toledo Assembly Complex, 4400 Chrysler Drive, Toledo, OH 43608. State WARN table rows: Toledo/Lucas, 1225, received 12/7/23; Toledo/Lucas, 1134, received 11/6/24. data/grants_raw.csv FY2018, FY2019, FY2020 and FY2021 rows. data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Aug and 2019-Jun rows.
notes: The payment addresses look wrong and are not. FY2018 and FY2020 were remitted to 8000 Chrysler Drive, Perrysburg, which is the Toledo Machining Plant in Wood County and FCA's local remittance address; FY2019 went to 1000 Chrysler Drive, Auburn Hills, Michigan; only FY2021 was remitted to 4400 Chrysler Drive, Toledo. JobsOhio's own project records put both projects in Lucas County, and FCA's only Lucas County plant is the Toledo Assembly Complex, which is exactly where both notices were filed. Two things to state plainly in the post. First, the plant did not close, so this is a mass layoff and not a closure. Second, 1,094 of the 1,225 in the 2023 notice are Supplemental Employees, that is temporary workers, so the 2024 notice of 1,134 is the stronger number to lead with because it is almost all permanent production staff and it came from cutting a shift. The June 2019 project claimed 5,164 jobs retained; the 2024 cut is about 22 percent of that.
funded_site: Toledo Assembly Complex, Lucas County (JobsOhio's 2017-Aug and 2019-Jun project records)
failed_site: Toledo Assembly Plant / Toledo South Assembly, 4400 Chrysler Drive, Toledo, OH 43608 (Lucas County)
recommend: Add to the count as a mass layoff at the funded site, using the 2024 notice of 1,134 as the headline figure and saying the plant stayed open.

name: ABC INOAC EXTERIOR SYSTEMS LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer on every notice is INOAC Exterior Systems, LLC at the payee's own address. The Schedule I payee is named ABC INOAC EXTERIOR SYSTEMS LLC, which was a joint venture of ABC Group and INOAC Corporation; by 2025 the letterhead and the signature block carry INOAC only. No bankruptcy.
ohio_outcome: The plant closed in stages through 2025. Thirteen separate notices were filed between 2025-01-17 and 2025-06-09, every one of them classed as a Closure by the state, all for 1410 Motor Ave, Fremont, OH 43420, and all signed by Cyle Hardymon, Human Resources Manager. The first and largest, received 2025-01-17, gives permanent job loss for 174 employees from about 2025-03-18: 92 assembly operators, 40 paint line operators, 17 injection machine operators, 10 polishers, 10 sanding operators, 2 forklift operators, 1 quality film technician, 1 materials buyer and 1 paint line supervisor. The twelve later notices run down the rest of the site, ending with a single Senior Paint Manager on 2025-08-08. The thirteen notices total 392 jobs. JobsOhio paid $67,647 in FY2022 and $94,811 in FY2023, $162,458 in all, to the same street address.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full: dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2025/INOACExteriorSystemsLLC1.pdf (received 1/17/2025, 174 employees, with the position schedule) and INOACExteriorSystemsLLC13.pdf (received 6/9/2025, 1 employee). All thirteen 2025 rows read from data/warn/notices.csv, each marked Closure: 174, 87, 78, 18, 11, 9, 5, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1. data/grants_raw.csv FY2022 and FY2023 rows (1410 MOTOR AVENUE, FREMONT, OH 43420). Corroborating headlines: Plastics News, 'Inoac Exterior Systems to close Ohio plant, relocate operations', 2024-11-01; WTOL, 'INOAC Exterior Systems in Fremont permanently laying off 174 employees', 2025-01-23; WTVG, 'Employees say INOAC plant in Fremont is set to close, laying off hundreds of workers', 2024-10-25.
notes: The brief listed this as a single notice affecting one person. It is thirteen notices for one staged plant closure, and the grant payee street on the Form 990, 1410 Motor Avenue, Fremont, is the exact address on every notice. The state labels all thirteen a Closure and the trade press reported a closure with operations relocating. Use the total of 392 or the largest single notice of 174, and say which; do not use the 1. The last cash payment was in FY2023 and the closure notices began about eighteen months later. No JobsOhio monthly-metrics project record was found for this company in data/commitments_norm.csv, so the county tie rests on the payee street rather than on JobsOhio's own project description.
funded_site: 1410 Motor Avenue, Fremont, OH 43420 (Sandusky County), the Schedule I payee address for both grant years
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed closure of the funded site, and correct the headcount to 392 across thirteen notices.

name: XELLIA PHARMACEUTICALS USA LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is Xellia Pharmaceuticals USA LLC, the grant payee itself, a subsidiary of Xellia Pharmaceuticals ApS. The event is the sale of the Bedford assets to Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. and the layoff of the workforce that went with it.
ohio_outcome: The funded plant shed its workforce in two waves and then was sold. On 2023-12-06 Xellia gave notice of a permanent mass layoff of about 80 employees at 200 Northfield Rd., Bedford, OH 44146, between 2024-02-05 and 2024-02-19, with a full job-title schedule running from aseptic operators to the plant engineer. On 2024-06-17 it gave notice that, in connection with the sale of its assets to Hikma, it anticipated a permanent layoff of about 247 US employees, 214 of them at the Bedford facility; a 2024-09-23 letter updated one separation date to 2024-12-31. A further 3-person notice followed on 2025-01-13. That is about 297 jobs at one site. JobsOhio's own records are three Cuyahoga County projects: January 2017, a $1,000,000 Workforce Grant with 170 jobs created and 10 retained on a $51,000,000 investment; March 2019, a $500,000 Revitalization Grant; and May 2019, a $700,000 Economic Development Grant with 100 created and 180 retained on a $21,753,000 investment. $2,200,000 was paid in cash, $1,000,000 in FY2018 and $1,200,000 in FY2020.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full: jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/XelliaPharmaceuticalsLLC.pdf (letter of 2023-12-06, 80 employees, three pages including the job-title table) and dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2024/XelliaPharmaceuticalsLLC.pdf (letter of 2024-09-23 updating the 2024-06-17 notice, naming Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. and the 214 Bedford employees). Both signed by Chris Eckerle, Vice President, Manufacturing Operations North America, Xellia Pharmaceuticals USA LLC, 200 Northfield Road, Bedford OH 44146. State WARN rows: Bedford Heights/Cuyahoga 80 received 12/6/23; Bedford/Cuyahoga 214 received 9/23/24; Bedford/Cuyahoga 3 received 1/13/2025. data/grants_raw.csv FY2018 and FY2020 rows (200 Northfield Road, Bedford, OH). data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Jan, 2019-Mar and 2019-May rows. Corroborating headlines: Fierce Pharma, 'Antibiotics specialist Xellia plots 247 layoffs on the heels of Ohio plant sale to Hikma', 2024-06-24; WKYC, 'More than 200 jobs to be cut at Bedford pharma manufacturing plant after Xellia Pharmaceuticals sells off assets', 2024-06-20; Cleveland.com, 'Former Ben Venue labs in Bedford sold again, leading to more than 200 layoffs', 2024-06-20.
notes: This is the cleanest match in the batch. The street on the Form 990 for both grant years, 200 Northfield Road, Bedford, is the exact street named in every notice, and JobsOhio's own project records are Cuyahoga County. The register labels the 2023 notice Bedford Heights and the 2024 notice Bedford; both letters give the same address, so that is a state data-entry difference and not two sites. The event is a sale plus a mass layoff, not a bankruptcy, and the post should say so. One date choice: use 2024-06-17, the date of the original notice quoted in the September update, rather than the September received date.
funded_site: 200 Northfield Road, Bedford, OH 44146 (Cuyahoga County), the Schedule I payee address for both grant years
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed sale and mass layoff at the funded site, with about 297 jobs across the three notices.

name: JO-ANN STORES
entity_filed: JOANN Inc., EIN 46-1095540, principal place of business 5555 Darrow Road, Hudson, Ohio, filed Chapter 11 twice. The grant payee, Jo-Ann Stores, LLC, EIN 34-0720629, is a co-debtor in both cases. The second case ended in a full liquidation.
court: Bankr. D. Del., Judge Craig T. Goldblatt
docket: 24-10418-CTG (JOANN Inc.), voluntary petition filed 2024-03-18; 25-10068-CTG (JOANN Inc.), voluntary petition filed 2025-01-15; co-debtor cases for Jo-Ann Stores, LLC and Jo-Ann Stores Support Center, Inc. in both
ohio_outcome: The funded site closed. JOANN's Omni Fulfillment Center at 1020 Enterprise Pkwy, West Jefferson, OH 43162, in Madison County, was the subject of a WARN notice dated 2025-01-24 and received 2025-01-27: 116 employees, separations from 2025-03-31, and 'the entire Omni FC will close'. The job-title schedule runs 25 detailers, 19 packers, 16 inventory control clerks, 13 group leads, 11 utility, 7 security officers and so on to the general manager. Those two amounts are exactly the $300,000 paid in FY2023 and the $500,000 paid in FY2024.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full: dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2025/JoAnnOmniFulfillmentCenter.pdf (letter of 2025-01-24, received 1/27/2025, naming 1020 Enterprise Pkwy, West Jefferson, and the 116-employee schedule, copied to the Madison County Board of Commissioners and the Mayor of West Jefferson) and JoAnnStoresSupportCenterInc2.pdf (the Hudson corporate office notice, 662). notes: This one nearly failed the site test and then passed it. The notice in the brief, 662 at the Hudson Support Center, is the corporate headquarters and is not the funded site: JobsOhio's own record is a Madison County distribution project, not a Hudson office project. Searching the register for Madison County turned up the right notice, the Omni Fulfillment Center in West Jefferson, 116 employees, which is the funded site and which closed. Use 116 and West Jefferson in the post, not 662 and Hudson, and name the Hudson closures only as context. The Schedule I street for both grant years is the Hudson tax department remittance address, which is why the address check alone would have pointed at the wrong site.
funded_site: Madison County distribution project, JobsOhio's 2021-May record; the Omni Fulfillment Center at 1020 Enterprise Pkwy, West Jefferson, OH 43162
failed_site: Omni Fulfillment Center, 1020 Enterprise Pkwy, West Jefferson, OH 43162 (Madison County)
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed Chapter 11 liquidation that closed the funded Madison County site, citing 116 jobs there rather than the 662 at the Hudson head office.

name: ATW OHIO LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The notice is from PJ Trailer Manufacturing Inc., described in the letter as 'a subsidiary of ATW', and is signed by Lynn Bates, Senior Vice President of Human Resources, American Trailer World Corp. ATW Ohio LLC is the Schedule I payee at the same street address.
ohio_outcome: The Mount Orab plant closed entirely. The notice dated 2026-09-08 and received 2026-09-09 gives formal notice of 'the planned permanent closure' of the facility at 200 Front Street, Mt. Orab, Ohio 45154, states that 'the entire Facility will close permanently', sets the closure date at 2026-11-08, and puts the total affected employees at 116 across production, safety, quality and leadership. The reason given is 'the economic realities of the market'. The letter says some Mount Orab employees may be able to transfer to the company's Big Tex Trailer plant in Batavia, Ohio, which stays open. JobsOhio's own May 2021 project record is ATW Ohio, LLC, Southwest region, Automotive, 249 jobs created and 137 retained on an $18,100,000 investment with a $300,000 Economic Development Grant; the county field reads 'Clermont &' and is truncated, so the project appears to span Clermont and Brown counties. $261,110 was paid in cash to ATW OHIO LLC in FY2022 and FY2023, and a further $300,000 was paid to AMERICAN TRAILER WORLD CORP, EIN 47-5665675, in FY2022, matching the $300,000 grant in the project record. The corporate family took $561,110.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2026/PJ_Trailer.pdf (letter of 2026-09-08 to the Rapid Response Unit, received 9/9/2026, plus the 2026-09-09 letter to plant employees). State current-year WARN row: PJ Trailer, Mount Orab/Brown, 116, Closure, layoff date 11/8/2026. data/grants_raw.csv FY2022 and FY2023 rows for ATW OHIO LLC (200 FRONT STREET, MT ORAB, OH 45154) and the FY2022 row for AMERICAN TRAILER WORLD CORP. data/commitments_norm.csv 2021-May row. Corroborating headlines: WKRC, 'Brown County community to lose over 100 jobs as manufacturing plant closes', 2026-09-15; Trucks, Parts, Service, 'Ohio Manufacturing Plant Closure: PJ Trailers Cuts 116 Jobs', 2026-09-21.
notes: The brief expected this to be a false match on the word 'trailer'. It is not. The notice names the same street as the Schedule I payee, 200 Front Street, Mount Orab, and is signed on American Trailer World letterhead; PJ Trailers is an ATW brand. The one qualification is the site split: JobsOhio's project record covers more than one county, and the notice itself says the Big Tex Trailer plant in Batavia, Clermont County, is still running and may take transfers. So the Brown County half of the funded project closed and the Clermont County half did not. Two things to carry into the post. First, the grant money to this family is $561,110 across two recipient rows, not $261,110, if the post counts by corporate family rather than by EIN. Second, 249 jobs were committed in 2021 and 116 were lost in 2026 at the plant the payee is named after.
funded_site: ATW Ohio, LLC, 200 Front Street, Mt Orab, OH 45154 (Brown County), the Schedule I payee address; JobsOhio's project record also covers Clermont County
failed_site: 200 Front Street, Mount Orab, OH 45154 (Brown County)
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed closure, and say the Brown County plant closed while the Clermont County plant in the same project stayed open.

name: DOREL HOME FURNISHINGS INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The notice is from Ameriwood Home (Dorel), signed by Raymond Toal, President, Dorel Home Furnishings Division. Dorel Home Furnishings Inc. is the Schedule I payee. The letter describes financial distress at the parent but no filing was made.
ohio_outcome: Manufacturing at the funded plant ended. The notice of 2024-07-08 says the Tiffin facility at 458 Second Ave, Tiffin, OH 44883, is being repurposed 'from a manufacturing operation to a Distribution and Warehouse Operation', that production equipment is moving to other Dorel plants, that the last day of production is 2024-09-05, and that about 40 hourly and salary jobs will remain as the Ohio Distribution Center. The stated reason is 'a significant downturn in our business' and that 'our parent company Dorel has been forced to make some hard financial decisions to survive this economy'. The letter says about 130 hourly employees are affected; the attached worker list is headed '154 Impacted Workers'; the state register records 130. Dorel later auctioned the entire contents of the plant and in August 2026 sold the building to Kreate Tiffin LLC for $13 million. JobsOhio's own September 2020 project record is Dorel Home Furnishings, Inc. in Seneca County, Advanced Manufacturing, 87 jobs created and 218 retained on a $3,270,000 investment, with a $325,000 Economic Development Grant and a $100,000 Workforce Grant. Those two amounts add to the $425,000 paid in cash in FY2023.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2024/DorelHome.pdf (letter of 2024-07-08, received 7/8/2024, plus the Dorel Home WARN Worker List). State 2024 WARN row: Dorel Home, Tiffin/Seneca, 130, received 7/8/24. data/grants_raw.csv FY2023 row (410 E First St S, Wright City, MO, $425,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2020-Sep rows. Corroborating headlines: Advertiser-Tribune, 'Ameriwood to close', 2024-07-16; WTOL, 'More than 100 employees laid off from Tiffin manufacturing facility', 2024-07-15; Woodworking Network, 'Dorel to auction the entire contents of its shuttered Ohio plant', 2025-09-11; GlobeNewswire, 'Dorel Industries Announces Sale of its Tiffin, Ohio Facility', 2026-08-13.
notes: The payment went to Wright City, Missouri, which is why the city-level join missed it; JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Seneca County and Tiffin is the county seat. Ameriwood Home is Dorel's trading name at Tiffin, and this is Dorel's only Ohio plant. Be precise about what happened: the manufacturing operation that JobsOhio paid for ended, and about 40 warehouse jobs stayed, so the honest description is the closure of the funded manufacturing operation rather than the closure of the whole site. The later auction and the 2026 sale of the building show the warehouse did not last either. The headcount is reported three ways, 130 in the letter and the state table and 154 on the attached worker list; use 130 and footnote the 154.
funded_site: Seneca County, Ohio (JobsOhio's 2020-Sep project record); the Ameriwood plant at 458 Second Ave, Tiffin
recommend: Add to the count as the confirmed end of the funded manufacturing operation, noting that about 40 warehouse jobs stayed on and the building was later sold.

name: CURATION FOODS INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The notice is from Curation Foods, Inc., the grant payee itself, signed by Lisa Rutkowski, Human Resources Director. Curation Foods is the renamed Apio, Inc., the subsidiary of Landec Corporation, now Lifecore Biomedical.
ohio_outcome: The funded plant closed completely, and JobsOhio got the money back. The notice dated 2022-01-11 and received 2022-01-18 says the company is closing 'its facility known as Curation Foods Bowling Green located at 12700 S. Dixie Hwy, Bowling Green, OH 43402', that 'the entire facility at this location is closing', that all employees at the facility will be terminated in the fourteen days from 2022-01-31, and that the closing is permanent with no transfer or bumping rights. The attached exhibit lists 110 jobs across 48 classifications, from the plant manager and division controller down to 11 warehouse labourers and the salads and beans lines. JobsOhio's own December 2017 project record for this operation is under the earlier company name, Apio, Inc., Wood County, Food Sciences and Agriculture, 150 jobs created and 176 retained on a $28,050,000 investment with a $350,000 Economic Development Grant. JobsOhio paid $350,000 in cash in FY2021 and then recorded minus $350,000 in FY2022, so the net cash to this recipient is zero.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Curation-Foods.pdf (letter of 2022-01-11, received 1/18/2022, with Exhibit A). State 2022 WARN row: Curation Foods, Inc., Bowling Green/Wood, 110, received 1/18/22. data/grants_raw.csv FY2021 row (12700 SOUTH DIXIE HIGHWAY, BOWLING GREEN, OH 43402, $350,000) and FY2022 row (29255 Network Place, Chicago, IL, minus $350,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Dec row for Apio, Inc.
notes: Two things make this row different from the rest. funded_site: 12700 South Dixie Highway, Bowling Green, OH 43402 (Wood County), the Schedule I payee address and JobsOhio's 2017-Dec Apio, Inc. project
failed_site: Curation Foods Bowling Green, 12700 S. Dixie Hwy, Bowling Green, OH 43402 (Wood County)
recommend: Add to the count as a confirmed closure of the funded site, but carry it at $0 and say JobsOhio recovered the $350,000 in the same year the plant closed.

name: MORGAN TRUCK BODY LLC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is Morgan Truck Body, LLC, the grant payee itself, headquartered at 111 Morgan Way, Morgantown, Pennsylvania. No bankruptcy.
ohio_outcome: A mass layoff at the funded plant, which stayed open. The notice of 2025-06-02 gives notice of a reduction in force at 'our facility located at 600 E. Chestnut Street, Orrville, Ohio, 44667', permanent, beginning 2025-08-01, affecting 110 employees with no bumping rights and no union. The attached schedule is almost all production: 40 production associates, 32 welders, 11 material handlers, 6 quality control, 6 work centre leads, 5 paint. JobsOhio's own June 2020 project record is Morgan Truck Body, LLC in Wayne County, Automotive, 139 jobs created and none retained on a $24,350,000 investment, with an $850,000 Revitalization Grant and a $150,000 Workforce Grant. Those two add to the $1,000,000 paid in cash in FY2023. The plant is still running: local coverage in August 2026 describes Morgan hosting a prototype showcase in Orrville.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2025/MorganTruckBodyLLC.pdf (letter of 2025-06-02, received 6/2/2025, with the affected-positions attachment), copied to the Mayor of Orrville. State 2025 WARN row: Morgan Truck Body, LLC, Orrville/Wayne, 110, Layoffs, layoff date 8/1/2025. data/grants_raw.csv FY2023 row (PO Box 27770, New York, NY, $1,000,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2020-Jun rows. Corroborating headlines: Wooster Daily Record, 'Morgan Truck Body lays off 110 workers in Orrville starting Aug. 2; city evaluates impact', 2025-06-06; News-Talk 1480 WHBC, 'Orrville Firm Announces 110 Layoffs', 2025-06-05; Assembly Magazine, 'Morgan Truck Body Expands With New Midwest Facility', 2019-07-22.
notes: The payment went to a New York lockbox, so the address check is no help; JobsOhio's own record puts the project in Wayne County and Orrville is in Wayne County. Confidence is Medium rather than High for one reason I could not close: no public document I could reach ties the $1,000,000 specifically to 600 E. Chestnut Street. The chain is circumstantial but tight. Morgan announced a new Midwest facility in 2019, JobsOhio recorded a Wayne County project in June 2020 with a Revitalization Grant, which is the programme for rehabilitating an existing building, and Orrville is Morgan's only Wayne County site. The Daily Record article and the Work Truck Online piece on Morgan's newer Ohio plant both refused automated fetches and had no Wayback snapshot, and the Assembly Magazine 2019 article URL is now a 404, so the opening date and address of the 2020 project are unverified. This is a layoff and not a closure: the plant was still operating in August 2026.
funded_site: Wayne County, Ohio (JobsOhio's 2020-Jun project record); Orrville is Morgan's only Wayne County facility
failed_site: 600 E. Chestnut Street, Orrville, OH 44667 (Wayne County)
recommend: Add to the count as a mass layoff at the funded site, flagged Medium confidence because no document names the street the $1,000,000 paid for.

name: Encore Industries Inc

ohio_outcome: The funded plant closed. The notice of 2023-09-12 says 'Encore Industries, Inc. is permanently closing its Cambridge facility located at 725 Water Street, Cambridge, Ohio 43725 effective November 12, 2023', affecting about 89 employees, with separations beginning the day of the notice and all accomplished by 2023-11-12, permanent, no union, no bumping rights, and some employees offered relocation or severance. JobsOhio's own August 2015 project record is Encore Industries, Inc. in Guernsey County, Advanced Manufacturing, 35 jobs created and 189 retained, with a $200,000 Economic Development Grant, which is the $200,000 paid in cash in FY2016.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/WARN 2023/Encore Industries Inc.pdf (letter of 2023-09-12, received 9/12/2023 at 2:55pm, copied to Mayor Thomas D. Orr of Cambridge). The PDF is a scanned image with no extractable text and was read by rendering the pages. State 2023 WARN row: Encore Industries, Cambridge/Guernsey, 89, received 9/12/23. data/grants_raw.csv FY2016 row (725 Water Street, Cambridge, OH 43725, $200,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2015-Aug row.
notes: The street on the Form 990 and the street in the closure notice are identical, 725 Water Street, Cambridge, and JobsOhio's project record is Guernsey County, so the site test is met twice over. The gap between the grant and the closure is long, seven years, which is worth stating rather than hiding: the 2015 project claimed 35 new jobs and 189 retained, and in 2023 all 89 remaining jobs went. The relocation offers in the letter suggest the work moved inside IPL rather than stopping.
funded_site: 725 Water Street, Cambridge, OH 43725 (Guernsey County), the Schedule I payee address and JobsOhio's 2015-Aug project county

name: Valeo North America Inc
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is Valeo North America, Inc., the grant payee itself, the US arm of Valeo SA of France. No bankruptcy.
ohio_outcome: Production ended at the funded plant. The notice, dated 2022-10-25 in the letter but received by the state on 2022-08-25, says Valeo North America, Inc. 'will be permanently laying off 104 employees between October 10, 2022 and October 24, 2022' and names the affected employment site as 'Valeo North America, Inc., 12979 County Rd 153, East Liberty, Ohio, 43319'. The attachment shows the whole site going, not a shift: 84 production operators, 5 supervisors, 4 quality technicians, 3 maintenance technicians, and single holders of the plant manager, production manager, quality manager, supply chain manager, human resources manager, engineer, logistics analyst and supply chain scheduler jobs. Plastics News reported it as 'Valeo ends production at Ohio plant, lays off 104'. $100,000 was paid in cash in FY2016 to the same street address.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Valeo-North-America-Inc-UPDATE.pdf (letter signed by Hanan Elgusain, Site Human Resources Manager, with Attachment A). State 2022 WARN row: Valeo North America, Inc., East Liberty/Logan, 104, received 8/25/22, layoff 10/10/2022 to 10/24/2022. data/grants_raw.csv FY2016 row (Valeo North America Inc, 12979 CR Road 153, East Liberty, OH 43319, $100,000). Corroborating headline: Plastics News, 'Valeo ends production at Ohio plant, lays off 104', 2022-09-08.
notes: The street on the Form 990, 12979 CR Road 153, East Liberty, and the site named in the notice, 12979 County Rd 153, East Liberty, are the same address. Because the entire management team is on the layoff schedule, including the plant manager, this reads as the end of the operation rather than a reduction, and the trade coverage calls it the end of production; the notice itself uses the words 'mass layoff' and not 'closure', so the post should say production ended rather than claim a formal plant closing. One gap: no JobsOhio monthly-metrics project record was found for Valeo in data/commitments_norm.csv, so there is no JobsOhio-stated county, jobs or investment figure for this grant and the site tie rests entirely on the Schedule I address. The letter also carries two conflicting dates, 2022-10-25 in the body and a received stamp of 2022-08-25; use the received date.
funded_site: 12979 CR Road 153, East Liberty, OH 43319 (Logan County), the Schedule I payee address
failed_site: 12979 County Rd 153, East Liberty, OH 43319 (Logan County)
recommend: Add to the count as the confirmed end of production at the funded site, and note that JobsOhio published no project record for this grant.

name: syncreon America Inc
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is syncreon America, Inc., the grant payee itself, described in the notice as 'a DP World company'. No bankruptcy.
ohio_outcome: A mass layoff at the funded operation, caused by its only customer. The notice of 2023-12-13 says syncreon 'intends to initiate a mass layoff at the plant operations located at 1515 Matzinger Road, Toledo, OH 43612', beginning about 2024-02-05, affecting about 68 employees: 41 operators, 17 forklift operators and 10 salaried. The stated reason is that 'our customer Stellantis only recently announced that it would be reducing a shift and insourcing a portion of the work at the Toledo operation', and that 'Stellantis is our only customer at the Toledo facility'. The separations are expected to be permanent and the employees are UAW Local 12. JobsOhio's own January 2018 project record is syncreon America Inc. in Lucas County, Logistics and Distribution, 8 jobs created and 277 retained on a $1,340,000 investment with a $150,000 Economic Development Grant, which is the $150,000 paid in cash in FY2018.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/WARN 2023/syncreonAmericaInc.pdf (letter of 2023-12-13 signed by Michelle Young, HR Director, with Nick Weber, HR Manager, at 1515 Matzinger Rd, Toledo). State 2023 WARN row: syncreon America, Inc, Toledo/Lucas, 68, received 12/14/23, layoff 2/5/24. data/grants_raw.csv FY2018 row (2851 High Meadow Cir, Auburn Hills, MI, $150,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2018-Jan row.
notes: The payment went to syncreon's Auburn Hills, Michigan head office, so the address check is no help; JobsOhio's record puts the project in Lucas County and the notice site is in Toledo, Lucas County. Confidence is Medium because no document names the street that the $150,000 paid for, and syncreon could in principle have had more than one Lucas County site; the project's profile, logistics and distribution with 277 jobs retained and only 8 created, fits a contract sequencing operation serving the Jeep plant, which is exactly what 1515 Matzinger Road is. Worth carrying into the post as a chain rather than two separate rows: the same Stellantis shift cut at the Toledo Assembly Complex that produced the FCA notice of 1,134 also wiped out this supplier's 68 jobs, and JobsOhio had paid both companies.
funded_site: Lucas County, Ohio (JobsOhio's 2018-Jan project record), a logistics operation with 277 jobs retained
recommend: Add to the count as a mass layoff at the funded site, and pair it with FCA to show one shift cut hitting two grant recipients.

name: BRANCH FINANCIAL INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The notice is from Branch Financial, Inc., the grant payee itself, signed by Pratiksha Patel, Chief People Officer. The company is still trading: Branch Insurance Exchange was publishing quarterly results in November 2025.
ohio_outcome: A 55-person layoff at a company that survived and kept being funded. The notice of 2023-06-05 says there will be a reduction in force at Branch Financial, Inc., that approximately 55 Ohio employees are included, that all affected employees will be notified on 2023-06-08, which is also their separation date, and that the separations are permanent. It also says 'We operate as a remote company; however, our headquarters are located at 20 E. Broad Street, Ste. 1200, Columbus, Ohio 43215. Most of the impacted employees work remotely from home.' JobsOhio kept paying after the layoff: $30,138 in FY2021, $146,732 in FY2022, $12,600 in FY2023 and $31,200 in FY2024, $220,670 in all, remitted to 875 N High Street, Suite 300, Columbus.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Branch-Financial-Inc.pdf (letter dated June 5 2022 in the body, which is a typing error for 2023 given the 2023 separation date and the 'Received June 5, 2023' stamp). State 2023 WARN row: Branch Financial, Inc., Columbus/Franklin, 55, received 6/5/23. data/grants_raw.csv FY2021 to FY2024 rows. Corroborating headlines: The Columbus Dispatch, 'Beam Dental, Branch Insurance cutting jobs', 2024-01-23; Coverager, 'Branch Insurance Exchange reports Q3 2025 results', 2025-11-25. No project record for this recipient appears in data/commitments_norm.csv.
notes: Three reasons not to call this a failure. The company is still operating, the layoff is 55 people at a remote-first business whose own notice says most of them worked from home rather than at any funded site, and JobsOhio paid it again in FY2024 after the cuts. There is also no JobsOhio project record in the monthly metrics for this recipient, so there is no stated county, job commitment or site to test the notice against; the Schedule I address, 875 N High Street, and the headquarters in the notice, 20 E. Broad Street, are two different Columbus addresses, which fits a company that moved. Confidence is Medium because the absence of a project record means the funded operation cannot be described precisely. If Eric wants this in the post at all, it belongs in a distress-but-survived category, not the failure count.
funded_site: Not established. No JobsOhio project record exists for this recipient; the Schedule I address is 875 N High Street, Suite 300, Columbus (Franklin County)
failed_site: Branch Financial, Inc., headquarters 20 E. Broad St., Ste. 1200, Columbus, OH 43215, with most affected employees working remotely
recommend: Keep out of the failure count; the company survived, JobsOhio paid it again afterwards, and the layoff was mostly remote staff.

name: ProMedica Health System Inc
ohio_outcome: The funded site is still open; the layoffs are at other sites and in a business ProMedica bought after the grant. JobsOhio's own published success story says what it paid for: 'In August 2017, nearly two years after announcing a major consolidation and revitalization project, ProMedica began moving nearly 1,000 employees into its new headquarters on Toledo's downtown riverfront', and 'ProMedica committed $60 million to revitalize an abandoned steam plant, constructed in 1896, to renovate a former KeyBank building and to reinvigorate Promenade Park along the riverfront'. That matches the October 2017 project record, Lucas County, Biohealth, 600 jobs created and 900 retained on a $46,360,000 investment with a $2,000,000 Revitalization Grant, and the $2,000,000 paid in cash in FY2018. Every WARN notice is somewhere else. The 2023-01-09 notice covers 255 remote senior-care staff assigned to the ProMedica Summit Center, 333 North Summit Street, Toledo, plus 7 who worked in that building; the 2023-03-15 and 2023-04-18 notices extend those same separations and follow from 'the divestiture of the majority of its skilled nursing facilities' on 2022-12-22. The 2023-05-31 notice closes the ProMedica Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation Sylvania Center at 5360 Harroun Road and the ProMedica Goerlich Memory Care Center at 5320 Harroun Road, Sylvania, 110 and 79 people. The 2023-10-17 notice cuts 122 at the ProMedica Home Health Agency, 5855 Monroe St., Sylvania, on 'the upcoming divestiture of the majority of its home health and hospice business'. A further 92 went at a Cleveland location in 2024.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full: jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Promedica.pdf (2023-01-09, Summit Center and remote senior care), Promedica-Update.pdf (2023-03-15, the five extension groups totalling 105), Promedica2.pdf (2023-04-18, the skilled nursing divestiture of 2022-12-22), Promedica3.pdf (2023-05-31, Sylvania skilled nursing and memory care, 110 plus 79) and jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/WARN 2023/ProMedicaEmploymentServicesII.pdf (2023-10-17, Sylvania home health, 122). Four of these are scanned images and were read by rendering the page images. JobsOhio's own success story at jobsohio.com/success-stories/promedica, published 2018-08-27, fetched and read. data/grants_raw.csv FY2018 row (1801 Richards Road, Toledo, OH 43607, $2,000,000). data/commitments_norm.csv 2017-Oct and 2018-Feb rows.
notes: This is the same shape as Dana, New Horizons and FedEx. JobsOhio paid $2,000,000 toward moving ProMedica's headquarters into the 1896 steam plant and the former KeyBank building on the downtown Toledo riverfront. What shed jobs in 2023 and 2024 was HCR ManorCare, the senior care business ProMedica acquired in July 2018, after the grant, and divested from December 2022: the former ManorCare head office at 333 N Summit Street, two Sylvania nursing homes, a Sylvania home health agency and a Cleveland office. None of those is the funded site, and I found no evidence that ProMedica has left the downtown headquarters. The brief listed the 6-person notice; the largest is 189 and it is in Sylvania, which fails the site test just as clearly. One residual gap: I did not independently check the current occupancy of the steam plant beyond a news search that turned up nothing about a move out.
funded_site: ProMedica's downtown Toledo headquarters, the 1896 steam plant and the former KeyBank building on the riverfront (JobsOhio's own success story and its 2017-Oct Lucas County project record)
failed_site: ProMedica Summit Center, 333 N. Summit Street, Toledo; 5360 and 5320 Harroun Road and 5855 Monroe St., Sylvania; and a Cleveland location
recommend: Reject. Keep it in the published reject list as a site-test case: the funded downtown headquarters is still open and the layoffs are in a senior care business bought after the grant.

name: ADS ALLIANCE DATA SYSTEMS
ohio_outcome: The closed site is not the funded site. The notice of 2021-01-13 says the layoff is 'prompted by the closure of Alliance Data's Credit Processing Center in Reynoldsburg, Ohio' and names the location as 'Alliance Data Card Services, 6939 Americana Parkway, Reynoldsburg, OH 43068', about 110 employees, with the centre permanently closed about 2021-10-31 and the work outsourced because 'significantly more cardmembers are choosing to pay their bills online instead of by mail'. The grant payee address is 3100 Easton Square Place, Columbus, OH 43219, and the company contact on the notice itself gives Alliance Data's own address as 3075 Loyalty Circle, Columbus, OH 43219, which is the Easton campus. JobsOhio's own January 2015 project record is ADS Alliance Data System Inc. in Franklin County, Financial Services, 700 jobs created and 1,300 retained on a $24,380,000 investment, with a $1,500,000 Economic Development Grant and a $500,000 Workforce Grant; those add to the $2,000,000 paid in cash in FY2017. A 700-job office expansion at Easton is not the long-standing mail-opening centre in Reynoldsburg.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/AllianceDataSystem.pdf (letter of 2021-01-13 from Alisha LaRochelle Danchak, VP Labor and Employment Counsel, copied to Mayor Joe Begeny of Reynoldsburg). State 2021 WARN row: Alliance Data Systems, Inc. (Alliance Data Card Services), Reynoldsburg/Franklin, 110, received 1/14/21. data/grants_raw.csv FY2017 row ($2,000,000 to 3100 Easton Square Place, Columbus) and FY2022 row (minus $250,000, 'PARCEL 010-146723', Columbus 43219). data/commitments_norm.csv 2015-Jan rows. Corroborating headlines: The Business Journals, 'Increased online bill pay leads to 110 Alliance Data job cuts in Reynoldsburg', 2021-01-14; 'New York investors pay $47M for Alliance Data headquarters building near Easton', 2018-08-07; 'Upstart doubling workforce to 1,000, leasing Alliance Data building in Easton', 2021-10-04.
notes: Reynoldsburg and the Easton campus are both in Franklin County, which is why the county fallback would pass this one. The street-level record does not. Confidence is Medium rather than High because no document I could reach states the address of the 2015 project; the inference rests on the payee street, the Easton address the company gave for itself in the notice, and the shape of the project, 700 new office jobs on a $24,380,000 investment. Two separate leads for someone else to pick up, neither of which this check can settle. First, data/grants_raw.csv records minus $250,000 against this recipient in FY2022, booked to a Columbus parcel number, so $250,000 of the $2,000,000 came back and the reason is not stated anywhere in the data. Second, trade coverage says Alliance Data sold its Easton headquarters building in 2018 and that Upstart leased an Alliance Data building at Easton in 2021, so the funded campus may have emptied out without a WARN notice.
funded_site: The Easton campus in Columbus, Franklin County: 3100 Easton Square Place on the Form 990, and 3075 Loyalty Circle as the company's own address in the notice
failed_site: Alliance Data Card Services Credit Processing Center, 6939 Americana Parkway, Reynoldsburg, OH 43068 (Franklin County)
recommend: Reject on the WARN evidence, but open a separate check on the $250,000 that came back in FY2022 and on whether the funded Easton campus was vacated.

name: THE SHERWIN-WILLIAMS COMPANY
ohio_outcome: A legacy plant closed while the funded project was being built. The notice of 2023-04-28 says 'The Sherwin-Williams Company will be closing its manufacturing facility located at 26300 Fargo Avenue, Bedford Heights, OH 44146', terminating all operations there, with production ceasing 2023-06-30 and up to 51 people, all those employed at that facility, losing their jobs; union employees are United Steelworkers. An amended notice of 2023-08-30 extends two separations to 2023-10-31. JobsOhio's own March 2020 project record is The Sherwin-Williams Company in Cuyahoga County, Energy and Chemicals, 400 jobs created and 3,524 retained on a $598,800,000 investment, with a $32,500,000 Economic Development Grant and a $5,000,000 Revitalization Grant. That is the new global headquarters in downtown Cleveland and the research and development centre, not a 51-person paint plant in Bedford Heights. $45,432,587 has been paid in cash across FY2023 to FY2025, every dollar of it remitted to 101 West Prospect Ave, Cleveland, which is the company's headquarters address and the address on the closure letter's own footer.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/Sherwin-Williams.pdf (letter of 2023-04-28 to Mayor Stanley C. Koci of Bedford) and jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/WARN 2023/Sherwin-Williams update.pdf (amended notice of 2023-08-30 to Mayor Fletcher Berger of Bedford Heights, signed by John S. Rossero, Sr. Director, Labor Relations). Both are scanned images and were read by rendering the page images. State 2023 WARN rows: Sherwin-Williams, Bedford Heights/Cuyahoga, 51, received 4/28/23; Sherwin-Williams - Updated, Bedford Heights/Cuyahoga, 2, received 8/31/23. data/grants_raw.csv FY2023 and FY2024 rows and data/grants_fy2025.csv FY2025 row, all to 101 West Prospect Ave, Cleveland. data/commitments_norm.csv 2020-Mar rows.
notes: The brief listed the 2-person amendment; the real notice is 51, and 51 is still the wrong operation. Bedford Heights is in Cuyahoga County, the same county as the funded project, so a county-level test passes and a site-level test fails. The point worth making in the post is not that this is a failure but that it is a mismatch of scale: Sherwin-Williams closed a 51-job plant in 2023 in the same county and the same years in which JobsOhio paid it $45,432,587 to build a new headquarters. That belongs in the story about grant size, not in the failure count.
funded_site: The new global headquarters in downtown Cleveland and the research and development centre, Cuyahoga County (JobsOhio's 2020-Mar project record); all payments remitted to 101 West Prospect Ave, Cleveland
failed_site: 26300 Fargo Avenue, Bedford Heights, OH 44146 (Cuyahoga County)
recommend: Reject from the failure count, but keep the pairing: a 51-job plant closed in the same county and the same years as a $45.4 million grant.

name: JSW STEEL USA OHIO INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The employer is JSW Steel USA Ohio, Inc., the grant payee itself, a subsidiary of JSW Steel Ltd. No bankruptcy.
ohio_outcome: Both 2020 notices are pandemic layoffs that the company itself expected to be temporary, and JobsOhio has funded the mill again since. The 2020-07-14 notice says the layoff of 160 at 1500 Commercial Avenue, Mingo Junction, 'is being done in conjunction with the temporary cessation of production at the facility due to unforeseeable business circumstances in connection with the current COVID-19 pandemic facing our nation', and 'We sincerely hope that this will be a temporary layoff of less than 6 months but are providing this notice pursuant to the WARN Act as a precautionary measure and as a good corporate citizen.' The 2020-04-09 notice of 162 uses the same language and cites stay-at-home orders. JobsOhio recorded a $4,000,000 Revitalization Grant for this Jefferson County mill in November 2018, 280 jobs created and 120 retained on a $270,000,000 investment, and then a further $2,000,000 JobsOhio Revitalization Grant in September 2023, 26 created and 400 retained on a $118,421,281 investment. Cash paid runs $2,500,000 in FY2020, $1,768,173 in FY2021, $169,773 in FY2022 and $800,006 in FY2025.
source: Ohio WARN notices fetched and read in full at jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/JSWSteelUSAOhio.pdf (2020-07-14, 160) and jfs.ohio.gov/static/warn/pdf/JSWSteelUSAOhioInc.pdf (2020-04-09, 162), both signed by Michael Sutfin, Vice President of Human Resources. State 2020 WARN rows: Mingo Junction/Jefferson, 160, received 7/14/20; Mingo Junction/Jefferson, 162, received 4/9/20. data/grants_raw.csv FY2020 to FY2022 rows and data/grants_fy2025.csv FY2025 row, all Mingo Junction. data/commitments_norm.csv 2018-Nov and 2023-Sep rows.
notes: The join flagged this because the covid_window flag was set on the April notice and left empty on the July one. Reading the July notice settles it: it says in terms that the layoff is a temporary cessation of production because of COVID-19. The site test passes, 1500 Commercial Avenue is the Schedule I address and JobsOhio's project county is Jefferson, but the event does not. The mill is still operating and JobsOhio paid another $800,006 in FY2025. One data fix to make: set covid_window on the 7/14/20 row in data/warn_join.csv so this does not resurface.
funded_site: 1500 Commercial Avenue, Mingo Junction, OH 43938 (Jefferson County), the Schedule I payee address and JobsOhio's project county
failed_site: Same site, but the event is a temporary COVID-19 production stoppage, not a failure
recommend: Reject, and set the covid_window flag on the 7/14/20 row in warn_join.csv so it does not come back.

name: PRIME AE Group Inc
ohio_outcome: No Ohio event for the payee. The notice is Washington Prime Group's, the Columbus-based shopping mall real estate investment trust spun out of Simon Property Group, and the register places it in Westerville, Franklin County, 139 affected, received 2025-04-02, classed as a Layoff. The PDF carries no letter, only the six-page schedule of job titles, and the titles are unmistakably a mall landlord's head office: SR DIR, Mall Accounting; SVP, Specialty Leasing; DIR, Specialty Leasing; RVP, Property Management; SR DIR, Joint Ventures; Lease Analyst, eighteen of them; Tenant Services Rep. There is no architecture or engineering role anywhere in the list. The payee is PRIME AE Group, Inc., an architecture and engineering firm at 8415 Pulsar Place, Columbus, OH 43240. Its JobsOhio project record is from May 2015, Delaware County, Information Technology, 59 jobs created and 83 retained on a $250,000 investment with a $75,000 Economic Development Grant, and its two payments are $54,212 in FY2016 for 'Conference expense support' and $20,788 in FY2018.
source: Ohio WARN notice fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN 2025/WashingtonPrimeGroup.pdf (six pages of job titles, received 4/2/2025, no cover letter). State 2025 WARN row: Washington Prime Group, Westerville/Franklin, 139, Layoff, 3/31/2026. data/grants_raw.csv FY2016 and FY2018 rows. data/commitments_norm.csv 2015-May row.
notes: The coordinator's suspicion was right. Two different companies that both reduce to the word 'prime'. There is nothing else in common: different industry, different city within Franklin County, different county in JobsOhio's record, and a grant purpose that is not even a site project. Worth keeping in the published reject list as an example of how a shared common word produces a false match in a name join.
funded_site: PRIME AE Group, Inc., 8415 Pulsar Place, Columbus, OH 43240; JobsOhio's project record is Delaware County, Information Technology
failed_site: Washington Prime Group, Westerville, Franklin County, an unrelated shopping mall REIT
recommend: Reject as a false match and keep it in the published reject list as an example of a shared-word collision.
